questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.topic: The Value of Denominations of Money
questions.learningObjective: Recall selected checked Nigerian banknote denominations and distinguish a denomination from a total made with several notes.
questions.prompt: Name three different Nigerian banknote denominations from the checked CBN list. Include the naira unit in each answer.
questions.answer: For example, ₦5, ₦100 and ₦500. Other distinct values in the checked list ₦5, ₦10, ₦20, ₦50, ₦100, ₦200, ₦500 and ₦1000 are acceptable.
questions.explanation: A denomination is the stated value of one note, not how many notes are held. This selected note-value task does not establish coin recognition or local circulation.

markingGuide.description: Names one valid banknote value with its unit.
Names a second different valid banknote value with its unit.
Names a third different valid banknote value with its unit.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.topic: The Value of Denominations of Money

questions.prompt: A fictional display uses three notes of denomination ₦20. A label says, The total is ₦60, so ₦60 must be a Nigerian banknote denomination. Calculate the total and explain the error in the label.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain a financial system through selected connections among institutions, markets, financial services and rules, rather than banknotes alone.
questions.prompt: Explain a financial system to a Primary 4 class using the idea of parts working together. Include one kind of institution and one activity those parts can support.
questions.answer: It is a connected arrangement of institutions, markets, services and rules that helps people manage and move funds. A bank is one institution; receiving savings or providing finance is an example of an activity.
questions.explanation: An age-appropriate explanation need not reproduce a technical definition. A bank is one part, not the entire system.

markingGuide.description: Explains connected parts rather than only physical money.
Names an appropriate financial institution.
Names a suitable financial activity.

questions.learningObjective: Explain a financial system through selected connections among institutions, markets, financial services and rules, rather than banknotes alone.
questions.prompt: A pupil says, A financial system is only a pile of naira notes. Use a bank and a capital market as examples to improve this explanation.
questions.answer: Notes are one form of money, but the system includes arrangements and organisations that provide services. Banks can receive savings or provide finance, and capital markets help channel funds through securities for longer-term needs.
questions.explanation: The source class content explicitly names banking and capital-market operations. This is a broad introductory comparison, not an exhaustive institutional map.

questions.prompt: In a fictional diagram, separate boxes say Savers, Bank and Borrowers, but no lines join them. What important idea is missing? Describe two labelled connections that would help explain the financial system.
questions.answer: The diagram omits relationships. One connection can show savers placing deposits with a bank; another can show the bank providing finance to borrowers who must repay as agreed.

questions.learningObjective: Describe selected saving, borrowing and capital-market operations using simple fictional examples and an actually produced infographic, without real transactions or guaranteed returns.
questions.prompt: In a fictional bank lesson, an adult puts money into an existing account and later takes some of that account’s money out. Name the two operations and explain the direction in which the account balance changes, ignoring fees and interest.
questions.answer: Putting money into the account is a deposit and increases its balance. Taking money out is a withdrawal and decreases its balance.

questions.prompt: A fictional company issues ordinary shares to raise funds. An investor buys some of those newly issued shares. What does the investor obtain, and how can this transaction help the company’s project?
questions.answer: The investor obtains a part-ownership interest in the company. The new issue raises funds that the company can use for its project.
questions.explanation: The question specifies a new issue; it does not incorrectly assume every later investor-to-investor trade sends fresh funds to the company. No return or management control is guaranteed.

markingGuide.description: Explains the part-ownership interest.

questions.prompt: A fictional company offers a bond described as a borrowing agreement with repayment terms. A pupil says that buying this bond must make its buyer an owner of the company. Explain the mistake using the relationship described.
questions.answer: The described bond makes the company a borrower and the buyer a lender/creditor. That debt relationship does not itself give the buyer an ownership share in the company.
questions.explanation: This is a simple debt/equity distinction, not legal advice or an assurance that a bond is risk-free or will be repaid.

markingGuide.description: Identifies a borrower–lender relationship.
Explains that the described debt does not itself create company ownership.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.subtopic: Selected dated banking and currency milestones
questions.learningObjective: Give a limited account of checked CBN1958/1959 and decimal-currency1973 milestones while distinguishing institutional history, currency change and full financial-system history.
questions.prompt: Put these selected milestones in time order and write a short account connecting them: introduction of decimal naira/kobo in 1973; the Central Bank Act of 1958; CBN full operations beginning on 1 July 1959. Do not say that these three events are the whole history of finance in Nigeria.
questions.answer: First came the 1958 Act, then CBN full operations began on 1 July 1959, and decimal naira/kobo was introduced in 1973. The law/operations concern an institution; 1973 concerns the currency units used. These are selected milestones, not the whole financial-system history.
questions.explanation: The anchors are crosschecked against CBN’s own history/gallery and historical Briefs. Dates for contested republic-related note changes and current legal requirements are not assessed.

markingGuide.description: Places the 1958 Act first.
Places full operations on 1 July 1959 next.
Places the 1973 currency change last.
Explains that the institutional and currency milestones concern different aspects.

questions.prompt: A historical display says that 50 kobo and ₦1 banknotes were among the notes introduced in 1973. A pupil copies that list as a complete list of today’s banknote denominations. questions.answer: The display describes one historical issue, not a complete present-day list. A value such as ₦100, ₦200, ₦500 or ₦1000 is in the checked current CBN list and absent from the pair.
questions.explanation: Do not infer a historical note’s present legal status from this task; no such status is established. Current value evidence is the separately registered CBN Legal Tender page.

markingGuide.description: Distinguishes the dated historical issue from a current complete list.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.subtopic: Selected dated banking and currency milestones
questions.learningObjective: Give a limited account of checked CBN1958/1959 and decimal-currency1973 milestones while distinguishing institutional history, currency change and full financial-system history.
questions.prompt: Two captions are proposed for a class history board: A, Nigeria’s financial system began only when the naira was introduced in 1973; B, The 1973 currency change was one milestone in a longer history that included CBN operations from 1959. Choose the better caption and explain the problem with the other.
questions.answer: B is better. A treats one change of currency as the beginning of all financial arrangements, even though the checked earlier 1959 CBN milestone already shows an institution operating before 1973.
questions.explanation: This is a limited chronology inference, not a claim that the system began in 1959. Earlier arrangements, wider banking/capital-market history and a complete documentary remain outside these drills.

markingGuide.description: Chooses B.
Explains why a currency change is not the beginning of all financial arrangements.
Uses the earlier 1959 milestone as evidence without saying all finance began then.
